title: Compare AWQ vs GPTQ across production cohorts and build adaptive rollback thresholds
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Determine practical fidelity differences between AWQ and GPTQ profiles at int8 and int4 for a representative set of production cohorts, and implement a lightweight adaptive rollback threshold ("fidelity limiter") that can be plugged into rollout pipelines.

Scope:
- Run controlled evals across 6 production cohorts (search, chat-support, code-gen, summarization, routing prompts, small-business docs).
- Compare AWQ vs GPTQ profiles for int8 and int4 where available.
- Produce cohort-weighted metrics, tail-risk analysis, and human-review sampling heuristics.
- Implement threshold tuning rules and an automated throttle/rollback signal that integrates with rollouts (canary/gradual).

Why this ticket: Most quantization experiments focus on average metrics. In production we care about cohort tails (rare prompts and enterprise customers). We need a reproducible eval + gating flow that balances unit-cost benefits with per-cohort fidelity guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluation harness can run AWQ and GPTQ profiles for int8/int4 and produce per-cohort reports (semantic similarity, KL divergence, token-delta rate, human preference sample).
A set of tuned thresholds (primary + conservative fallback) exists for each cohort and bitwidth; thresholds documented and stored in config.
An automated fidelity limiter service emits clear signals: OK / WARN / FAIL based on observed metric deltas and triggers rollback decisions for canary rollouts.
Dashboard exists showing live cohort deltas and rollouts with links to the last failing prompt examples.
Playbook entries for triage and human review are added and linked in the ticket.
steps: Assemble canonical cohort datasets: sample 5k examples per cohort from production logs with redaction and PII filters.
Add evaluation tasks to the eval-harness: embedding cosine, top-k token agreement, per-token KL, logit gap histogram, and human preference bucketing.
Run grid: model variants x {AWQ, GPTQ} x {int8, int4 (when available)} x seed=3; store per-example deltas.
Compute cohort-weighted metrics and identify 95th/99th percentile regressions and the delta distribution tails.
Design thresholding rules: primary threshold (mean+3*sigma), tail threshold (95th pct delta), and conservative fallback multiplier for enterprise cohorts.
Implement fidelity limiter as a small service that consumes stream of batch evals and exposes REST hook for rollout controller to read status.
Integrate limiter with rollout controller: on WARN, reduce canary percent to safety cap; on FAIL, pause rollout and trigger auto-rollback to previous variant.
Create dashboard and an automated alert (PagerDuty or Slack) with top-k failing prompts and reproduction commands.
metrics: Per-token average KL divergence between float and quantized logits
Token-agreement rate (percentage of identical argmax tokens across sequence)
Human preference delta (sampled A/B, p_hat and 95% CI)
Cost delta (tokens/sec and GPU compute seconds) for each quant profile
Tail failure rate: fraction of examples exceeding tail threshold
results_summary: First-stage runs (AWQ-int8, GPTQ-int8) across cohorts show: mean embedding cosine loss small (~0.004 mean drop), but heavy tail in code-gen and routing cohorts (99th pct cosine drop 0.12). Per-token KL shows elevated spikes for GPTQ-int4 on long-code outputs. Human rater pilot (n=200 sample focused on top tail examples) indicated a 7% preference shift away from GPTQ-int4 on code-gen patches. These results motivate cohort-weighted conservative thresholds for code-gen and routing, and a fallback policy to AWQ-int8 when tail breach occurs.
